A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProxyAttn by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, attention and prefilling speed measurements, and ablations, including detailed results in Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds attention-sink controls in Section 5.5 and observational results across synthetic and real-world data in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Proxy-head pooling, strided score estimation, block-aware dynamic budgets, and sparse-mask construction remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. Sink-token removal is an observational control, not a modification to ProxyAttn.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same RULER, InfiniteBench, and LongBench-v2 coverage. Appendix E examines attention on already represented RULER and LongBench-v2 data; removing sink-token attention scores is an internal diagnostic, not a new input task or environment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in corresponding benchmark, efficiency, and ablation experiments. SharePrefill is newly discussed in related work but is not evaluated against ProxyAttn.

E3.justification: Section 5.5 adds observational controls excluding four sink tokens, with and without attention renormalization. Appendix E extends shared-ranking observations across selected layers and heads on two retained datasets. Existing benchmark settings and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted tests of whether inter-head similarity is driven by attention sinks and whether shared rankings behave consistently across synthetic and real-world data. Existing head-count, budget-allocation, scaling, and hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe averaging speed measurements over multiple runs across layers without specifying run counts. v2 adds no seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 and existing plotted results remain unchanged, including the 10.3x attention and 2.4x prefilling speedup claims. New Figures 6–8 report residual head overlap after sink removal and similar shared-ranking behavior across RULER and LongBench-v2.

T1.justification: The method equations and computational-cost reasoning are retained. New Equation 4 restates the top-1024 cumulative-attention overlap metric already described in v1 Section 2.2. The correction from 'MN' to 'M,N' is not a substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free proxy-head estimation, dynamic budgets, accuracy, and acceleration. The added diagnostics support those claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 newly interprets residual overlap as evidence that proxy-head usefulness extends beyond shared sink tokens. Appendix E interprets similar cumulative curves across both domains as supporting generality. These extend the mechanism discussion without revising existing limitations.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added diagnostics through the four-token removal setting, renormalization condition, and dataset, layer, and head selections shown in Figures 6–8. Core implementation details, hardware, method hyperparameters, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Xiao et al. (2023) on attention sinks and Peng et al. (2025) on SharePrefill. Section 6 acknowledges SharePrefill's related use of inter-head similarity through offline clustering and sparse-pattern sharing, modestly expanding research positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. Changes comprise Section 5.5, Appendix E, a short related-work addition, acknowledgements, updated contact and conference-header text, and a small notation correction.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 6, which repeats the original overlap display alongside two sink-removal conditions, and Figures 7–8 with layer-wise cumulative curves. Existing figures and table designs are retained; appendix tables shift position and conference headers are added.

improvement.justification: v1's motivating observations leave attention sinks and transfer beyond the illustrated synthetic example insufficiently examined. Section 5.5 and Appendix E provide targeted evidence addressing both concerns, while the SharePrefill discussion improves related-work coverage. These additions strengthen the method's empirical rationale, although they remain illustrative and leave the main quantitative evaluation unchanged.
